### The Covenant-Making God
Author: Michael A. Youssef, Ph.D.
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-devotional-for-january-19-2026.html
Passage: Genesis 15:17-18
Points:
- Abraham needed reassurance after waiting ten years in Canaan without children or land.
- God met Abraham where he was by initiating a familiar ancient covenant ceremony using divided animal sacrifices.
- While ancient pacts required both parties to pass through the carcasses, God alone moved between the pieces.
- By walking through the halves alone, God took the curse upon Himself to guarantee the promise unconditionally.
- This covenant commitment found its ultimate fulfillment at the cross, where Christ secured eternal salvation for believers.

### Abram's Question
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/abrams-question
Passage: Genesis 15:8
Points:
- Abram asked how he could know he would possess the land, taking God's self-imposed obligation seriously.
- Even great saints experience imperfect faith and need divine help when wrestling with doubt in this life.
- Unlike unbelievers who allow doubt to turn them away, believers bring their struggles to God and seek confirmation in His Word.
- God sustains struggling believers through preaching, the sacraments, and supportive accountability within Christian fellowship.

### Help for Our Unbelief
Author: Mark Ross
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/help-our-unbelief
Passage: Genesis 15:1-21
Points:
- Long trials and delayed fulfillment can cause believers to feel as though their faith is slipping.
- God did not react with anger to Abram's plea for certainty, but instead responded with tenderness and patience.
- In the covenant ceremony, God passed between the pieces to pledge His own life to the fulfillment of His promise.
- God elevated His promise into a sworn oath so His people would have strong encouragement to hold fast to hope.
- Believers receive that same covenant assurance today at the Lord's Table through the signs of Christ's sacrifice.
